source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 23, Table E (MFJ/QSS, more than 24,000 to 30,000: .75; more than 30,000 to 30,500: .70); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 30,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income = 30,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 0.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 30,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 30,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 30,000.00 - 0.00 = 30,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 30,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 30,000.00 is not more than 48,000.00, exemption 24,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 30,000.00 - 24,000.00 = 6,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 6,000.00: 6,000.00 x 0.02 = 120.00 = 120.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 30,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 120.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.75 (Connecticut AGI 30,000.00 is in the band more than 24,000.00); Line 9 = 120.00 x 0.75 = 90.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 120.00 - 90.00 = 30.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut AGI exactly 30,000, the projection's threshold: Table E bands are 'More Than / Less Than or Equal To', so 30,000 is still in the .75 band; the .70 decimal starts only above 30,000.
